ICSE 2027 (Synthetic Fixture) Paper #8 LogLens: Summarizing Incident Logs for On-Call Engineers
===========================================================================

Review #8A [r2]
===========================================================================

Overall merit
-------------
2. Weak reject

Reviewer expertise
------------------
Y. I am knowledgeable in this area.

Paper summary
-------------
Paper present LogLens, a tool that summarize incident logs for on-call engineers with a small language model fine-tuned on 3,000 incidents from one company.

Detailed comments for authors
-----------------------------
The user study has only 8 engineers and all from same company. I would like to see a comparison with the summaries that engineers write by hand today.

Review #8B [r2]
===========================================================================

Overall merit
-------------
2. Weak reject

Reviewer expertise
------------------
Y. I am knowledgeable in this area.

Paper summary
-------------
In an era where software systems are increasingly complex, incident response has never been more critical. This paper introduces LogLens, a groundbreaking approach to log summarization.

Strengths
---------
The approach is not merely a summarizer. It is a paradigm shift in how teams handle incidents. The writing is clear, concise, and compelling.

Detailed comments for authors
-----------------------------
The user study includes only eight engineers, which is a significant limitation. As noted earlier, all participants come from a single company. It is worth noting that the generalizability of the findings remains an open question.

The paper would benefit from a comparison with hand-written summaries and a discussion of the cost of fine-tuning the model for a new company with different log formats.

Review #8C [r2]
===========================================================================

Overall merit
-------------
2. Weak reject

Reviewer expertise
------------------
Y. I am knowledgeable in this area.

Paper summary
-------------
LogLens fine-tunes a 1.3B model on 3,000 incidents and generates a summary of the first ten minutes of each incident log, which the authors compare with a keyword baseline and with GPT-4.

Detailed comments for authors
-----------------------------
The ROUGE scores in Table 2 favor the fine-tuned model, but the user study shows no difference in time to diagnosis, and the paper should discuss what the ROUGE gains mean for the engineers.

Please release the anonymized incidents or explain why this is not possible, and report the inference time on the hardware that an on-call engineer would have available. It would also help to state whether the model runs on a laptop without a GPU, since many teams cannot send incident logs to a cloud service.
